questionText:
Read the following excerpt on Kshitindranath Majumdar's masterpiece 'Rasa-Lila' and answer the questions that follow:

Painted in 1926 by Kshitindranath Majumdar, 'Rasa-Lila' is one of the most spiritually radiant and lyrical achievements of the Bengal School wash tradition. Majumdar, who was revered as a 'Bhakta-Shilpi' (Saint-Artist) for his lifelong devotional immersion in the Chaitanya Mahaprabhu Vaishnava faith, translates the mystical Maha-Rasa of Vrindavana into a celestial visual reverie. In the painting, Lord Krishna dances in a harmonious ring with the cowherd maidens (Gopis) in a sacred grove under the silvery glow of the full moon. Majumdar's figures are distinguished by their extraordinary elongated grace, slender willow-like waists, and sinuous undulating lines that sway with musical cadence. The flowering branches of Kadamba trees drape over the dancers, framing the ecstatic circular dance against translucent, pastel washes of pale mauve, soft saffron, and dusky blue, conserved in the National Gallery of Modern Art, New Delhi.

questionText:

When the Constituent Assembly of India completed drafting the Constitution of the Republic of India, Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru personally invited Nandalal Bose and his master students from Kala Bhavana, Santiniketan, to illustrate the original calligraphed manuscript. Working between 1949 and 1950, Nandalal executed 22 monumental header panels for the 22 parts of the Constitution, visually chronicling 5,000 years of Indian civilizational history. Each illustration was carefully chosen to reflect the spirit of the corresponding constitutional text: Part III on Fundamental Rights is headed by Lord Rama, Sita, and Lakshmana returning victoriously to Ayodhya; Part IV on Directive Principles of State Policy depicts Lord Krishna preaching the Bhagavad Gita to Arjuna on the battlefield; and other sections feature seals from the Indus Valley Civilization, the Vedic ashram, Gautam Buddha, Lord Mahavira, Emperor Ashoka, Emperor Akbar, Chhatrapati Shivaji, Rani Lakshmibai, Mahatma Gandhi's Dandi March, and Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose.
